The aca tax credits will expire before they can be voted on. Under House rules (as outlined in Clause 2 of Rule XV and related procedures), once a discharge petition obtains 218 signatures:

The petition is placed on the Discharge Calendar.
Seven legislative days must elapse before a signer can announce intent to call up the discharge motion.
The motion can then be offered on the second or subsequent legislative day after that announcement, and the Speaker must schedule it within two legislative days thereafter.

A legislative day is any day the House is in session (not calendar days).
The House was in session through December 19 or 20, 2025, before adjourning for the holiday recess, with plans to return around January 6, 2026. This means insufficient legislative days remained in December to complete the seven-day waiting period.
As a result, the earliest the floor vote can occur is in January 2026, likely the second week (mid-January), when the House reconvenes and accumulates the required legislative days.
Speaker Johnson could theoretically bring it up sooner by scheduling the bill voluntarily or bypassing some procedural hurdles, but he has opposed the ACA extension and shown no indication of doing so. Reports indicate the vote is not expected before January 2026 at the earliest.
